scientific_scope_status: A covalently attached donor handle retained after a complete denaturing wash can witness a new covalent connection under the stated graph/isolation assumptions, but wrong-site bonds and orientation still alias. With IID rebuilt children and node acceptance q=p+f independent of size/protocol, balanced L=2^k fusion has expected consumption(2/q)^k leaf units before processing overhead; accepted-product purity needs independent correct-junction factors(p/q)^(L-1). Product-length-dependent q can restore exponential cost. Odd A-ended completed AA/BB fragments cannot terminally CuAAC-cyclize, yet the unmasked bridge has only1/6 correct endpoint pairs in the symmetric toy. Independent-clock clean-completion bounds and a verified1023-label code provide separate conditional tools, not a physical writer.

located_proof_sources.quote: DECISIVE FAILURE OF THE UNMASKED BRIDGE: In the bridge step, each A-ended input fragment exposes two A ports, while B has two identical B ports. There are four candidate A ports; only two are intended: left fragment's right port and right fragment's left port. In a symmetric sequential without-replacement port-selection toy model, there are C(4,2)=6 equally probable endpoint pairs. One creates correct fusion, two consume both termini of the same fragment and make a ring, and three create wrong orientations/crosslinks. Therefore correct=1/6, ring=1/3, other wrong=1/2. This is not a prediction of real collision rates, but demonstrates that safe completed endpoints DO NOT ensure safe ternary fusion.
